q: Two of the six Cognac crus carry the word Champagne in their names. Which of them ranks highest?
exp: Both sit on chalky soils that give long-lived, floral spirit. A bottle labelled Fine Champagne blends the two, with at least half from Grande Champagne.

q: How many times must Cognac go through the still, and in what apparatus?
opts: Three times, in a pot still
Twice, in a Charentais pot still
exp: The second pass, the bonne chauffe, is where the cuts are made. Armagnac by contrast traditionally takes a single pass through a column of its own design.

q: A label reads VSOP. What is the minimum age of the youngest spirit in that blend?
exp: VS requires two years and VSOP four. Age statements on blended spirits always describe the youngest component, never the average.

q: Gascony distils its brandy traditionally in a single pass through a small continuous column of local design. Which spirit is that?
exp: The alambic armagnacais delivers a lower-strength, more aromatic and more rustic spirit. Bas-Armagnac is the most admired subregion, and single-vintage bottlings are a local tradition.

q: Normandy fills its stills with something that is not a grape at all. What comes out?
opts: Pear brandy, sold as poire williams
exp: Cider is distilled, with pears permitted alongside apples. Pays d'Auge is the appellation that insists on double distillation in pot stills.

q: Which requirement must every Scotch satisfy before it can legally be sold?
opts: Distillation three times in pot stills
Ageing in new charred oak barrels only
Three years in oak casks in Scotland
exp: Three years in oak in Scotland and a minimum of 40 percent alcohol are the baseline. Any age on the label refers to the youngest whisky in the bottle.

q: A bottle says single malt. What exactly does the word single promise?
opts: That it all came from one distillery
That it went through the still only once
That it came from one cask
That only one grain besides barley was used
exp: Single means one distillery, not one barrel; the contents are usually a blend of many casks. A one-barrel bottling is labelled single cask separately.

q: Smoke, tar and medicinal iodine in a malt whisky are picked up at which point in production?
opts: When the malt is dried over peat
From sea water added before bottling
exp: Burning peat coats the damp malt in phenolic compounds that survive all the way to the glass. Islay is the classic home of the style, though peating is a choice, not a place.

q: Which grain has to make up at least 51 percent of the mash bill for a whiskey to be called bourbon?
exp: The balance is usually rye or wheat plus a little malted barley for enzymes. Wheated bourbons read softer and rounder; high-rye ones read spicier.

q: Casks used to mature bourbon can be filled only once. What kind are they?
exp: That one-fill rule floods the world with cheap ex-bourbon barrels, which is why Scotch, Irish whiskey, rum and tequila so often mature in them.

q: Before it goes into the barrel, a Tennessee whiskey is filtered through a deep bed of sugar maple charcoal. What is that step called?
exp: The charcoal strips harsher compounds from the new spirit and is what separates Tennessee whiskey from bourbon. Sour mash, by contrast, means recycling spent stillage into the next mash.

q: Triple distillation and a generally unpeated character are most associated with which country's whiskey?
exp: Irish whiskey also has a category of its own in single pot still, made from a mash of both malted and unmalted barley, which gives a distinctive creamy, spicy weight.

q: Which single agave species is permitted for tequila?
exp: Tequila is restricted to one plant, grown chiefly in Jalisco. Mezcal may draw on many species, of which espadin is by far the most planted.

q: The harvested heart of the plant is trimmed of its spiked leaves before cooking. What is that heart called?
exp: It is named for its resemblance to a pineapple and can weigh well over forty kilograms. The plant takes several years in the ground before it is ready to cut.

q: A tequila has spent five months in oak. Which category does that put it in?
exp: Blanco is essentially unaged, reposado runs from two to twelve months, anejo from one to three years and extra anejo beyond three.

q: Where does the smoke in most mezcal come from?
exp: Roasting in wood-fired earthen pits is the defining step and puts smoke into the sugar before fermentation even begins. Tequila steams its agave in ovens or autoclaves, which is why it is not smoky.
